scope: Hodgson-linked paper-pulp transfers with material/package state, route infrastructure, and pre-existing Company transport metrology.
central_claim: The March 1842 twenty-four-package pulp shipment entered a transport corridor that was already both physically and administratively structured. By 1825 the Company listed Govindgunge as an up-river boat-hire destination with a standardized two-month allowance and priced baggage boats by carrying capacity and monthly rate. Rankine's 1838 report shows the physical constraints behind such standards. Actual 1842 route, freight cost and Serampore relation remain unresolved.

shipments.recipient_transcript_exact: G. Woodcock Esq., Joint Magistrate, Champaun

route_alternatives.decision_variable: relative water carriage cost and safety

physical_infrastructure_context.source: Robert Rankine, Notes on the Medical Topography of the Districts of Sarun, report 22 Jan 1838, print 1839
observations: Great and Little Gunduck navigable for small boats but navigation capacity variable
Govind Gunge and Bettiah roads included in bad-road discussion
high road to Chumparun hardly passable in many places five or six months per year
poor cross-roads could increase reliance on human carriage and raise cost
physical_infrastructure_context.use_rule: context only; does not establish actual pulp route or carrier

route_metrology_context.source: The New Annual Bengal Directory and General Register, 1825, Rates of Boat Hire
route_metrology_context.scope: Time allowed for boats to proceed to listed destinations as per Company's allowance, plus baggage-boat capacity/monthly-rate schedule
route_metrology_context.rate_control: exact table visually verify before detailed quantitative publication

place_name_control.rule: retain exact source spelling in transcription fields

multi_metrology_model.interpretation: Material circulation becomes administratively actionable through multiple non-equivalent metrologies layered around the object. Package count does not equal mass; route allowance does not equal observed duration; boat capacity does not reveal the actual boat used.

source_control_rules: Do not use 1825 two-month allowance as actual 1842 transit duration.
Do not claim the 1825 allowance remained unchanged in 1842 without later rules or the actual freight bill.
Do not infer boat capacity from 24-package count.
Do not infer package mass from Company baggage-boat categories.
Keep standard allowance, actual time, standard rate and actual cost separate.
Keep Govindgunge/Govind Gunge/Govind Gang exact strings in source fields.
Keep the Serampore consignment edge unproven.
